conflicts: 6p lifetimes: the only direct measurement, 55(4) ns for both 6p1/2 and 6p3/2 (Zaki Ewiss et al. 1983), is below the values derived from the 410 nm Stark shift plus theory, 63.77(50) and 58.17(45) ns (Safronova et al. 2013) and CCSD(T) 63.8(8) / 58(1) ns; the derived values are probably better.

nd 2D lifetimes: beam-foil (Andersen & Sorensen 1972: 7d 50(5) ns) disagrees by factors 3-4 with pulsed-laser values (Jonsson et al. 1983: 7d3/2 200(4), 7d5/2 147(10) ns; Zaki Ewiss & Snoek 1983: 7d5/2 154(10), 8d3/2 317(22) ns); all-order theory (42-77 ns) sides with beam-foil but does not include the 5s5p2 perturber. Laser values are used as main entries.
7s lifetime: 19.5(1.5) ns (Zaki Ewiss) versus 27(6) ns (Jonsson et al.).
6s lifetime: 7.0(3) (Norton & Gallagher), 7.4(3) (Havey et al.), 7.5(7) ns (Andersen & Sorensen); theory 7.04 (SD) and 6.6(2) (CCSD(T)).

5d hyperfine constants: experiment A(5d3/2) = -64(1), A(5d5/2) = 151.2(9) MHz (Vernon et al. 2020) versus all-order SD theory -11.48 and 47.83 MHz (Safronova et al. 2007); theory nd hyperfine values were therefore left out for 6d-8d.
6p1/2 hyperfine splitting: 1257.0(5) MHz (Augenbraun 2016) differs by 6 MHz from George et al. 1990.
Abundance / moment values differ slightly between sources (mu(115In) 5.5326(4) on the UDel portal, 5.5408(2) in Garcia Ruiz et al. 2018: with/without diamagnetic correction).
not_found: Lande g_J factors (measured) for In I levels: NIST ASD lists none; no source opened.
Absolute (frequency-comb) frequencies of the 410.2, 451.1 and 325.6 nm lines: none located; Kim, Haubrich, Meschede, Opt. Express 17, 21216 (2009) full text could not be opened.
Isotope shift of the 325.6 nm cooling line 5p3/2-5d5/2 as a transition value: only level isotope shifts of 5d (Vernon 2020) and 5p3/2 (272(6) MHz) were found.
Measured hyperfine constants of 113In for 6p, 7s; of either isotope for 7p, 6d, 7d, 8d; Zimmermann (1970) 5d5/2 level-crossing values not opened.
Measured lifetime of the metastable 5p 2P3/2 level (theory 10.4(2) s only).

Measured transition probabilities beyond NIST for the 5p-ns, nd lines (Penkin & Shabanova oscillator strengths are only quoted in Safronova 2007 Table IV and were not transcribed because of column ambiguity).
Original papers of Eck/Kusch (B constants), Jackson 1981, Neijzen & Donszelmann 1980, George et al. 1990, Zaal et al. 1978: values are second-hand.
notes: Both stable isotopes have I = 9/2 (115In is very weakly radioactive, 95.71%). Hyperfine entries from Garcia Ruiz et al. 2018 carry statistical (A_unc) and systematic (A_unc_sys) uncertainties separately. level_isotope_shift_MHz is the shift of the level itself (113In minus 115In centroid, relative to the ionization limit) as tabulated by Sahoo et al. 2019 / Vernon et al. 2020. Transition isotope shifts keep the printed convention: keys "115-113" mean nu(115)-nu(113). rme_J_ea0 values are theory unless noted: "CC" = linearized coupled-cluster (Safronova, Safronova, Porsev 2013), sqrt(S) values derived from the all-order SD line strengths of Safronova, Safronova, Kozlov 2007 (same convention as the schema: A = 2.02613e18 S/((2J'+1) lambda^3)). The 6s-6p matrix elements and 6p lifetimes marked derived come from the measured 410 nm Stark shift (Ranjit et al. 2013) plus theory. Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: level_isotope_shift_MHz, natural_linewidth_MHz, stark_shift_kHz_per_kVcm2, C_MHz (magnetic octupole), *_unc_sys, ionization_energy, mu_N. The UDel portal has no neutral In entry (only In+).
